person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio - A MARKER IN WIDE CLINICAL USE WITH NO REFERENCE RANGE, whose cut-offs had been taken from the diseased populations it was meant to identify
span.quote: However, which NLR value is correlated with a higher risk for these patients? Which cut-off value, for the NLR, will discriminate normal from abnormal results? Different values of NLR, with different methods, in different populations (cancerous or not) are cited in the literature. And finally, no universal value is currently available. Therefore, there is a need for reference values to progress in the use of this marker.

span.label: what values of the NLR occur in an adult, non-geriatric population without acute illness or chronic debilitating disease
span.quote: The aim of this study is to determine the limits of the values of the NLR that are observed in an adult, non-geriatric population, without any acute illness and/or chronic debilitating disease.

span.label: an upper and lower reference limit for the NLR derived from healthy subjects rather than from patients, with an independent validation cohort
span.quote: We have identified that normal NLR values in an adult, non-geriatric, population in good health are between 0.78 and 3.53. These data may help the researcher as the clinician searching for a cut-off for the NLR, until now lacking.

span.label: existence
span.quote: We have identified that normal NLR values in an adult, non-geriatric, population in good health are between 0.78 and 3.53. These data may help the researcher as the clinician searching for a cut-off for the NLR, until now lacking.

span.label: a ratio of two routinely-counted cell populations used as an inflammatory index, whose distribution in health had not been described
span.quote: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is a simple parameter to assess easily the inflammatory status of a subject.

span.label: 413 routine blood samples from workers in a health-care prevention programme, log-normal statistics, mean +/- 1.96 SD with 95% CI; validated against 29 strictly selected healthy controls run on four further analysers
span.term: 413 routine blood samples from workers in a health-care prevention programme, log-normal statistics, mean +/- 1.96 SD with 95% CI; validated against 29 strictly selected healthy controls run on four further analysers
span.quote: For the statistical analyses, laboratory parameters fit a log-normal distribution. Logarithmic conversion was therefore used for calculating means and 95% confidence limits (95% CI) are presented as arithmetic mean ± 1.96 SD (with their 95% CI). Power analysis shows that, to test the hypothesis that <2.5% of the normal controls would be out of the proposed limits, 28 subjects are needed. It is the reason why we included 29 blood samples of the historical cohort for the external validation.

span.label: THE CUT-OFF WAS DERIVED FROM THE POPULATION IT WAS MEANT TO DISTINGUISH, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO: `NONE OF THESE STUDIES BASED THEIR CUT-OFF ON DATA COMING FROM POPULATION IN GOOD HEALTH, and none on data coming from normal controls. Some of these studies chose their cut-off value ON THE BASIS OF THE MEDIAN, HIGHER QUARTILE OR VALUES DETERMINED BY THE USE OF RECEIVER-OPERATING CURVES`. A marker whose whole job is separating sick from well, thresholded from the median of the sick
span.quote: Nevertheless, none of these studies based their cut-off on data coming from population in good health, and none on data coming from normal controls. Some of these studies chose their cut-off value on the basis of the median, higher quartile or values determined by the use of receiver-operating curves (to predict the occurrence of a condition, e.g. cancer recurrence of infection)

span.label: and the field had no single number at all: `Different values of NLR, WITH DIFFERENT METHODS, IN DIFFERENT POPULATIONS (cancerous or not) are cited in the literature. And finally, NO UNIVERSAL VALUE IS CURRENTLY AVAILABLE`. Three sources of variation named in one sentence - the value, the method and the population
span.quote: However, which NLR value is correlated with a higher risk for these patients? Which cut-off value, for the NLR, will discriminate normal from abnormal results? Different values of NLR, with different methods, in different populations (cancerous or not) are cited in the literature. And finally, no universal value is currently available. Therefore, there is a need for reference values to progress in the use of this marker.

span.label: the correction is a change of REFERENCE CLASS, not of statistic: `IN CONTRAST WITH THESE STUDIES, we found here limits based on a sample of AN ACTIVE ADULT POPULATION IN GOOD HEALTH`. Same arithmetic, different people, and that is the whole paper
span.quote: In contrast with these studies, we found here limits based on a sample of an active adult population in good health. This value can be used as a cut-off to differentiate patients that are in the range of a population in good health or not

span.label: THE PAPER'S OWN HEADLINE NUMBER IS STATED TWO WAYS. The upper reference limit is the entire contribution, and it appears FIVE TIMES AS 3.53 - abstract, Results, Table 1 and both Conclusions - and ONCE AS 3.58, in the Discussion: `the NLR values, in a sample of 413 active subjects in good health, are BETWEEN 0.78 AND 3.58`. VERIFIED AS THE PUBLISHER'S TEXT, not the pipeline's: `3.58` occurs once in the source XML and `3.53` five times, same file, same renderer
span.quote: We show here that the NLR values, in a sample of 413 active subjects in good health, are between 0.78 and 3.58. We confirm that no normal control (selected on the basis of the absence of any comorbidities and substance abuse, including tobacco) exceeded this range.

span.label: AND `HEALTHY` IS DEFINED BY WHAT WAS NOT RECORDED: the samples come from `workers POTENTIALLY EXPOSED TO X-RAYS OR ANY OTHERS IONIZING RADIATION`, anonymised such that `NO INFORMATION WAS THEREFORE AVAILABLE ABOUT HABITS (e.g. tobacco use) AND POSSIBLE COMORBIDITIES (e.g. obesity or vascular disease)`. The reference class for normal is `held a full-time job and nothing was written down`
span.quote: Blood samples were obtained for routine hematologic control in workers potentially exposed to X-rays or any others ionizing radiation. Samples were treated anonymously, including sex and date of birth. No information was therefore available about habits (e.g. tobacco use) and possible comorbidities (e.g. obesity or vascular disease).

span.label: and health is operationalised as EMPLOYABILITY: `these subjects were in good health, PERMITTING A FULL TIME JOB WITHOUT RESTRICTION, and without any active disease ... and are REPRESENTATIVE OF THE POPULATION AS A WHOLE` - a representativeness claim made for a working-age, occupationally-screened sample
span.quote: Typically, these subjects were in good health, permitting a full time job without restriction, and without any active disease, including cancer and infectious disease and are representative of the population as a whole.

span.label: the paper lists what its own range cannot cover: `AGE IS CERTAINLY A LIMIT, as we tested only adult, non-geriatric, subjects (between 21 and 66 years) ... ETHNIC GROUP ORIGINS, SEX AND SEASON OF ASSESSMENT HAVE NOT BEEN INCLUDED IN THE ANALYSES`
span.quote: Can it be used in other populations that this from which this sample is coming? Age is certainly a limit, as we tested only adult, non-geriatric, subjects (between 21 and 66 years). Additionally, we did not have the complete documentation of substance use/abuse, like tobacco or oral contraceptive. Ethnic group origins, sex and season of assessment have not been included in the analyses.

span.label: FIVE ANALYSERS, FIVE MEANS - 1.65, 1.76, 1.86, 1.68, 1.69 - a 13% spread reported as agreement: `the NLR values are in the same range, WHICHEVER THE USED ANALYZER`. True of the RANGE and not of the mean, and the reference limits come from one instrument
span.quote: Results coming from the blood samples of the 413 subjects of the main cohort are presented in Table 1 . Briefly, the mean NLR is 1.65 [±1.96 SD: 0.78–3.53] (95% CI [0.75–0.81] and [3.40–3.66]). In the second cohort (healthy control), the NLR values are in the same range, whichever the used analyzer (Table 1 ). Consequently, no NLR assessed in the validation series is out of the proposed limits.

span.label: a second, independent cohort of 29 subjects selected on strict health criteria - no chronic disease, no substance or medication use including tobacco - run on four further analysers
span.note: eliminates: the objection that the main cohort's limits reflect its own unscreened population: `no NLR assessed in the validation series is OUT OF THE PROPOSED LIMITS` · outcome: held
span.quote: Our goal is to identify the higher boundary observed in a population in good health, but not excluding non-debilitating disease, tobacco use or oral contraception. Therefore, it would be important to compare the results to those obtained in a second, and independent, sample (n = 29) of normal controls, strictly selected on the basis of perfect health, coming from an historical cohort. This cohort was used during the process of the calibration of the blood analyser. The subjects in this second cohort were in the same range of age, but, after interrogation and examination, carefully selected on the basis of the absence of any chronic disease or substance/medications (abuse, including tobacco use).

span.label: a stated power calculation for the validation cohort - `to test the hypothesis that <2.5% of the normal controls would be out of the proposed limits, 28 SUBJECTS ARE NEEDED. IT IS THE REASON WHY WE INCLUDED 29`
span.note: eliminates: the objection that n=29 was chosen for convenience; the number is derived and the derivation is printed · outcome: held
span.quote: For the statistical analyses, laboratory parameters fit a log-normal distribution. Logarithmic conversion was therefore used for calculating means and 95% confidence limits (95% CI) are presented as arithmetic mean ± 1.96 SD (with their 95% CI). Power analysis shows that, to test the hypothesis that <2.5% of the normal controls would be out of the proposed limits, 28 subjects are needed. It is the reason why we included 29 blood samples of the historical cohort for the external validation.

span.label: NLR sample stability over 48 h
span.note: eliminates: pre-analytical drift as a source of the observed spread - `there was no significant variation over this time period and the NLR was then considered stable` · outcome: held
span.quote: NLR sample stability over 48 h was assessed; there was no significant variation over this time period and the NLR was then considered stable.

span.quote: We have identified that normal NLR values in an adult, non-geriatric, population in good health are between 0.78 and 3.53. These data may help the researcher as the clinician searching for a cut-off for the NLR, until now lacking.

span.label: the Discussion's version of the same upper limit; the publisher's text, verified against the source XML
span.quote: We show here that the NLR values, in a sample of 413 active subjects in good health, are between 0.78 and 3.58. We confirm that no normal control (selected on the basis of the absence of any comorbidities and substance abuse, including tobacco) exceeded this range.

span.label: the lower reference limit, consistent everywhere in the paper
span.quote: We have identified that normal NLR values in an adult, non-geriatric, population in good health are between 0.78 and 3.53. These data may help the researcher as the clinician searching for a cut-off for the NLR, until now lacking.

span.label: subjects in the main cohort, from a workplace health-care prevention programme
span.quote: Results coming from the blood samples of the 413 subjects of the main cohort are presented in Table 1 . Briefly, the mean NLR is 1.65 [±1.96 SD: 0.78–3.53] (95% CI [0.75–0.81] and [3.40–3.66]). In the second cohort (healthy control), the NLR values are in the same range, whichever the used analyzer (Table 1 ). Consequently, no NLR assessed in the validation series is out of the proposed limits.

span.label: subjects in the validation cohort - 28 were required by the power calculation
span.quote: For the statistical analyses, laboratory parameters fit a log-normal distribution. Logarithmic conversion was therefore used for calculating means and 95% confidence limits (95% CI) are presented as arithmetic mean ± 1.96 SD (with their 95% CI). Power analysis shows that, to test the hypothesis that <2.5% of the normal controls would be out of the proposed limits, 28 subjects are needed. It is the reason why we included 29 blood samples of the historical cohort for the external validation.
